items_missed: Never asked 'How are you today?' — jumped straight from greeting into qualifying the lead
Never used the customer's name (Amy) a single time after collecting it

No Save Your Ass prep speech — no 'prep before move day = shorter move = lower bill' framing, no consolidation list (kids' toys, garden tools, loose drawer items, photos off walls), no 'take a carload' tip, no 'does that make sense?' close. Only a single tacked-on tip about emptying the dresser, framed as damage prevention rather than time/cost savings, and delivered after the booking was already closed
Never captured the destination zip code (only the street address)
Never asked about a storage unit stop (asked about garage storage only)

Estimate variables not explained: stairs at the two-story destination, the antique art / large dresser / bookshelf as specialty-item time drivers, walk distance, and no equivalents (school bus reference) to make the volume tangible
Packing pricing not clearly explained — quoted '$217' for packing without stating that packing labor bills at the same hourly rate plus materials
No mention of the BOLDED detail list at the top of the confirmation email
No 'reply with any corrections' ask — customer was never asked to verify the details in the email
Business hours never given (only 'email, call, or text us anytime')
Insurance explanation incomplete — No Worries $2,000 covered, but no 60¢/lb baseline coverage contrast
top_strength: The pricing block was excellent and near-complete — 'super simple' opener, day-of-week hourly tiers ($104 Tue-Thu vs $110 Friday), the full inclusions list, trip fee, all three differentiators (No Worries, Meet Your Mover, On-Time Guarantee), the no-hidden-fees pitch, and the entire clock explanation with a sense-check, delivered in one clean uninterrupted stretch. She also asked for the business directly — 'Would you like me to lock that in for you?' — and closed a two-day pack-and-move booking.
coaching_note: Add the Save Your Ass prep speech before the booking ask, not after it. Roselyn had the perfect setup — Amy volunteered a large dresser and a bookshelf as her only concerns, and Roselyn even said the final bill 'depends on how well prepared you are.' But she never turned that into the actual speech: prep before move day means a shorter move and a lower bill, here's what to consolidate (kids' toys, garden tools, loose items in drawers, photos off the walls), and anything small can go in your car. On a two-day full-pack job billed hourly, that speech is the single biggest lever on this customer's bill and on the estimate-accuracy gap — and it lands far better before the close than as an afterthought.
phone_presence_notes: Polite and professional with one nice repeat-customer touch ('thank you so much for considering us once again'), but transactional overall — zero name use, heavy 'Mm-hmm' filler, and the customer's fragile-items mention got a clipped acknowledgment rather than any reassurance.
audio_review_reason: Transcript is heavily garbled in the rep's delivery ('already weight' for hourly rate, 'sterle fees', 'bunds', 'for December', '4th of April' self-corrected to September, 'north Queensland park road' for Quinlan Park). Clarity was scored as a miss, but audio is needed to separate genuine rep mis-speaking and mis-hearing from ASR error.
